requiredbulletpoints.bulletpoint: Unity software engineer on two shipped VR titles—Virtual Virtual Reality 2 and the licensed Stranger Things VR—developing gameplay systems, rhythm engine technology, and platform integrations across Meta Quest, Rift, and SteamVR.

bulletpoints.bulletpoint: Contributed gameplay systems and narrative cutscene implementation for Stranger Things VR, including major sequences in the Spider Monster level and dreamscape encounters. Implemented interactive telekinetic mechanics, environmental interactions, and portions of enemy AI behavior for the Meta Quest release.

Maintained and extended existing cross-platform input and tutorial systems for Virtual Virtual Reality 2, ensuring consistent behavior across Meta Quest, Rift, and SteamVR following team transitions and supporting stable multi-device releases.

Designed and fully implemented a reusable VR rhythm game engine for Virtual Virtual Reality 2, owning all gameplay systems and delivering 4 new levels in a 3-month Music Update cycle. Engine supported variable tempo changes, generalized map structures (note types, metadata), and sustained 72 FPS performance on Meta Quest 2 hardware.

Extended and productionized an internal subtitle generation system supporting 7 languages, adding validation tooling to detect missing or broken characters and improve localization coverage, reducing manual verification effort and improving release reliability.

Worked within Meta’s FQA certification process for a high-visibility licensed title, resolving platform compliance issues and resubmitting fixes within 1–5 day verification cycles to ensure release readiness under Meta’s publishing standards.
